articles.title: High Court Trial Begins Over Ownership of Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A two-day trial in Manchester's High Court will determine the future of Hopwood Hall, as Hopwood DePree seeks to reclaim his ancestral home from Rochdale Council.
articles.content_html:
A trial concerning the ownership of Hopwood Hall commenced today at the High Court in Manchester, with Hopwood DePree contesting Rochdale Council's ownership of the historic manor house. DePree, a descendant of the Hopwood family who built the manor in the 1420s, claims the council has reneged on an agreement that would allow him to purchase the property.

The hall, which has been owned by Rochdale Council since it was bought from private owners in the 1980s, is a Grade II-listed building that has suffered from neglect and disrepair. DePree has spent seven years working with the council to restore the site, aiming to secure its future and potentially repurpose it for community use.

In November 2024, the council ended its exclusivity agreement with DePree, stating that no commercially viable business model had been presented for the hall's restoration. DePree argues that the council's decision contradicts earlier agreements made when planning permission was granted in 2022, which he believes should trigger the transfer of ownership.

The outcome of this trial could significantly impact the future of Hopwood Hall, which is currently situated within the grounds of Hopwood Hall College. The court's decision is expected to clarify the legal standing of the property and the potential for its restoration.
